findings: The transparent side gutters read cleanly at the reviewed 2x runtime size; no visible green fringe or edge contamination was observed. Manifest validation also reports alpha, transparent corners, and zero visible-green fraction.
No stray opaque black block or text-like mark is visible. The near-black center is coherent forged-iron material rather than an artifact; OCR is empty.
The palette is consistent with dark iron and restrained aged gold. Gold highlights are narrow and subdued, with no bright-yellow flare.
At a 12 CSS px by 128 CSS px repeat unit, the rail does not read as excessively thick or bright; it remains subordinate to page content.

Top and bottom cuts keep the same silhouette and apparent alignment, with no cap, flare, or crossbar. A repeat-y join is visually plausible, but the single-tile review cannot prove a multi-tile seam is invisible; the recorded 2x top/bottom color RMSE of 0.0294538 leaves a small phase or brightness seam risk.
integrationConstraints: Render the reviewed 24x256 2x file at exactly 12x128 CSS px with background-size: 12px 128px and repeat-y; do not stretch, crop, rotate, or use cover or contain.
Anchor the rail and repeat origin on integer CSS pixels at DPR1 and DPR2; avoid fractional transforms and offsets that can introduce interpolation or a synthetic seam.
Preserve the transparent side gutters and place the asset over the shared dark shell material; do not add glow, brightness, saturation, or gold-tint filters.
Keep the rail decorative and non-interactive with pointer-events disabled, outside content geometry.

Before any production promotion, verify at least three consecutive repeats in the selected non-home canary at DPR1 and DPR2, inspecting both junctions on the real shell background. Reject or regenerate the asset if either junction reads as a horizontal brightness or texture seam.
This review authorizes canary integration only; it does not establish route fidelity or production registry promotion.
